package.title: Tempo.Blazor
package.description: Comprehensive Blazor component library with 100+ components. Supports WebAssembly, Server, and InteractiveAuto render modes. Multi-targets .NET 8/9/10. Includes multilingual support (EN/CS), CSS variable theming, and dark mode. Optional FluentValidation integration is available through Tempo.Blazor.FluentValidation.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started with Tempo.Blazor
gettingStarted.overview: Tempo.Blazor is a comprehensive Blazor WebAssembly component library providing 100+ UI components for building modern web applications. It includes inputs, forms, data tables, pickers, charts, layout, navigation, feedback, workflow designer, scheduler, and more. All components use the Tm prefix (e.g., TmButton, TmDataTable).
gettingStarted.platform: Blazor WebAssembly, Blazor Server, and InteractiveAuto (hybrid rendering)

renderModes.description: Tempo.Blazor supports all Blazor render modes.

modes.name: InteractiveWebAssembly
modes.description: Full client-side rendering in the browser via WebAssembly.

modes.name: InteractiveServer
modes.description: Server-side rendering with SignalR connection for interactivity.

modes.name: InteractiveAuto
modes.description: Starts with Server rendering, switches to WebAssembly once downloaded. Recommended for best UX.

renderModes.notes: Components with JS interop (dashboard, workflow designer, rich editor, scheduler, PDF viewer, diagram editor, color picker, file manager, Gantt, Notion editor, document editor, signing, spreadsheet, wireframe designer, and email variable insertion) gracefully degrade during prerendering and activate once the client-side runtime is available.

cssFramework.description: Tempo.Blazor uses its own standalone CSS framework based on CSS custom properties (design tokens). No external CSS framework (like Bootstrap or Tailwind) is required. The library ships a single tempo-blazor.bundled.css file that includes all component styles, design tokens, base resets, and animations.
cssFramework.architecture: The CSS is organized as: tokens (design variables) → base resets → component styles. Each component uses BEM-like class naming with the tm- prefix (e.g., tm-btn, tm-data-table, tm-modal__header).

darkMode.description: Dark mode is supported via CSS custom property overrides. Activate by adding data-theme="dark" attribute or .tm-dark class to a parent element (typically <html> or <body>).
darkMode.themeService: Use the ThemeService (registered via DI) to toggle themes programmatically.

designTokens.description: All visual properties are controlled via CSS custom properties (--tm-*). Override these to customize the look and feel without modifying component CSS.

colorPrimary.description: Primary brand color palette (blue by default)

borders.description: Border colors. --tm-border-color is the decorative divider tone; the boundary of a selection control (checkbox, radio, multiselect option), which conveys the control's state, uses --tm-border-color-control so it stays above the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 minimum. Retheming a control must go through the -control token, not through --tm-border-color. --tm-control-hover-fill is the fill an UNCHECKED control takes while hovered: the hover used to recolour the outline only, which is a hue change of ~1.05:1 and therefore invisible in greyscale. A palette override must keep the hovered outline (--tm-color-primary) at 3:1 against this fill.

typography.description: Font families, sizes, weights, and line heights

tokens.--tm-font-mono: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Code', 'Source Code Pro', Menlo, monospace

customization.description: Override design tokens in your app CSS to customize the theme globally.

localization.description: Tempo.Blazor supports localization via the ITmLocalizer interface (namespace Tempo.Blazor.Localization, defined in Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions). All built-in component UI strings (button labels, tooltips, placeholders, validation messages, aria-labels, etc.) go through this interface. The library ships with 500+ localization keys covering all components.

architecture.interface: ITmLocalizer — two indexer overloads: this[string key] for simple lookups, this[string key, params object[] arguments] for formatted strings (e.g. Loc["TmImageGallery_Counter", 5, 20] → "5 of 20").
architecture.defaultImplementation: DefaultTmLocalizer (internal) — backed by IStringLocalizer<TmResources> using embedded .resx files (TmResources.resx for English, TmResources.cs.resx for Czech).
architecture.injection: All components get the localizer via @inject ITmLocalizer Loc in the library's _Imports.razor. Components then use Loc["KeyName"] in markup and code.
architecture.registration: AddTempoBlazor() registers: (1) ITmLocalizer as Singleton (stateless, thread-safe, backed by .resx), (2) ThemeService as Scoped (per-circuit in Server, per-tab in WASM), (3) ToastService as Scoped (per-circuit in Server, per-tab in WASM). Uses TryAdd* so your custom registrations take precedence if registered AFTER AddTempoBlazor().

localization.keyNamingConvention: Keys follow the pattern Tm[ComponentName]_[Action/State]. Shared keys use Tm_ prefix (e.g. Tm_Save, Tm_Cancel, Tm_Loading). Component-specific keys include the component name (e.g. TmDataTable_NoResults, TmRichEditor_Bold, TmFilterBuilder_Contains).

keyCategories.shared: Tm_Loading, Tm_Close, Tm_Cancel, Tm_Save, Tm_Delete, Tm_Confirm, Tm_NoResults, Tm_Error, Tm_Retry, Tm_Search, Tm_Clear, Tm_Select, Tm_SelectAll, Tm_DeselectAll, Tm_Edit, Tm_Add, Tm_Remove, Tm_Apply, Tm_Reset, Tm_Previous, Tm_Next, Tm_Download, Tm_Upload, Tm_Create, Tm_Optional, Tm_Required, Tm_Yes, Tm_No
keyCategories.dataTable: TmDataTable_NoResults, TmDataTable_Loading, TmDataTable_PageSize, TmDataTable_SearchPlaceholder, TmDataTable_ShowingItems, TmDataTable_SelectAll, TmDataTable_DeselectAll, TmDataTable_BulkActions, TmDataTable_ExpandAll, TmDataTable_CollapseAll, TmDataTable_GroupDropPlaceholder
keyCategories.richEditor: TmRichEditor_Bold, TmRichEditor_Italic, TmRichEditor_Underline, TmRichEditor_Undo, TmRichEditor_Redo, TmRichEditor_InsertLink, TmRichEditor_InsertImage, TmRichEditor_InsertTable, etc. (56 keys total)
keyCategories.filterBuilder: TmFilterBuilder_Equals, TmFilterBuilder_NotEquals, TmFilterBuilder_Contains, TmFilterBuilder_StartsWith, TmFilterBuilder_Between, TmFilterBuilder_GreaterThan, TmFilterBuilder_LessThan, TmFilterBuilder_In, TmFilterBuilder_NotIn, etc.
keyCategories.pickers: TmDatePicker_Today, TmDatePicker_Clear, TmTimePicker_Hours, TmTimePicker_Minutes, TmDateRangePicker_LastWeek, TmDateRangePicker_LastMonth, TmDateRangePicker_ThisYear, etc.
keyCategories.other: TmAlert_Dismiss, TmButton_Loading, TmSearchInput_Placeholder, TmNotificationBell_*, TmViewManager_*, TmDashboard_*, TmPasswordStrength_*, TmActivity_*, TmTimeline_*, etc.

switchLanguage.description: Set the culture in Program.cs before builder.Build(). This makes IStringLocalizer pick the correct .resx file automatically.

customLocalizer.description: To fully replace all component strings (e.g. for a language not shipped with the library), implement ITmLocalizer and register it AFTER AddTempoBlazor(). The TryAddSingleton in AddTempoBlazor() will be skipped if your registration comes first.

partialOverride.description: To override only specific keys while keeping the rest from the built-in resources, create a decorator that falls back to the default implementation.

addNewLanguage.description: To add a new language (e.g. German), implement ITmLocalizer with all keys translated. You can export the English .resx keys as a reference. Since DefaultTmLocalizer is internal, a full custom implementation is the recommended approach for new languages.

items.description: Internal helper component that renders the formatting toolbar for TmRichEditorFull and TmRichEditorSimple. Operates in two modes: Simple (basic formatting, lists, links, emojis) and Full (adds headings, strikethrough, subscript/superscript, indent/outdent, code, blockquote, horizontal rule, text/highlight colors, image, table, video, remove format). Not intended for direct use.

parameters.description: List of currently active formats.

parameters.description: Whether the toolbar is disabled.

parameters.description: Optional free-text filter forwarded to the timeline tab (author, content, entry type).

parameters.description: Page size for the timeline tab's incremental "load more" paging. null (default) shows every entry.

items.description: Displays a chronological timeline of activity entries (comments, status changes, assignments, attachments) with author avatars, relative timestamps, and color-coded connector dots per entry type. Entries are sorted newest-first.

parameters.name: DataProvider
parameters.description: Optional async data provider. When set, entries are fetched (filtered + paged) from it instead of Entries.

parameters.name: Entries
parameters.description: Timeline entries to display. Sorted newest-first. Ignored when DataProvider is set.

parameters.name: EntryTypeFilter
parameters.description: Optional entry-type filter (e.g. "comment"); null/empty shows all types (additive, default: none).

parameters.name: EntryTypeFilterOptions
parameters.description: Optional explicit set of entry-type options for the filter bar. When null, distinct types are derived from Entries.

parameters.name: Filter
parameters.description: Optional free-text filter applied to author, content, and entry type (additive, default: none).

parameters.name: IsLoading
parameters.description: Whether the timeline is loading data.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description: Page size for incremental "load more" paging. null (default) shows every entry — backward compatible.

parameters.name: ShowFilterBar
parameters.description: When true, renders a built-in search + type filter bar (default: false).

parameters.name: ShowInternal
parameters.description: Whether internal entries are included (default: true — the activity timeline shows everything).

examples.title: Basic timeline

examples.title: With ref for programmatic refresh

items.description: Block-based WYSIWYG markdown editor (Notion-inspired). The user edits rich formatted content — bold, italic, headings, lists, links, code — with no markdown syntax ever visible. The Value parameter is a raw Markdown string (input and output). Internally each paragraph, heading, or list item is a separate block div; inline formatting uses real semantic HTML elements (<b>, <em>, <s>, <code>, <a>). Supports Ctrl+Enter submit, character limit, link dialog, and keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+K).

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class applied to the root container element.

parameters.name: IsDisabled
parameters.description: Disables the editor and the entire toolbar.

parameters.name: MaxLength
parameters.description: Maximum number of characters allowed. 0 = unlimited. Shows a character counter in the footer when set.

items.description: Pure SVG chart component supporting Bar, Line, Area, Pie, Donut, and HorizontalBar chart types with optional legend, grid, value labels, animation, gradient area fills, a proportional DateTime X axis for time series, combo charts (per-dataset ChartDataset.RenderAs = ChartDatasetRenderAs.Line renders that dataset as a line overlay over the bars of a Bar chart on a shared Y scale — bars for periodic flows, lines for cumulative values), dense-axis label thinning on Bar charts (over 24 categories only every n-th label renders), negative values on Bar/Line charts (signed domain with an emphasized zero axis; bars grow down from the zero baseline), point-marker thinning on dense line series (markers closer than ~9 units thin to ~24-unit spacing while the polyline stays complete), and click events on segments. Chart types additionally include Funnel (conversion trapezoids with per-stage conversion percentages), Heatmap (dataset-rows × label-columns intensity matrix with a global scale), Treemap (squarified shares, flat or hierarchical via ChartTreeNode), and Waterfall (the first value starts at zero and subsequent values are cumulative deltas, with optional connectors and calculated total). Stacked variants (StackedBar vertical, StackedHorizontalBar, StackedArea) accumulate each category's datasets on a shared baseline scaled to the largest stack total; non-positive values contribute nothing to a stack, datasets toggle off through the series legend, and bar value labels are omitted when a segment is too small to keep the text readable.

parameters.name: AreaGradient
parameters.description: Area charts only: fills each series with a vertical gradient fading from the series color to transparent instead of the flat token-driven fill. Default false.

parameters.name: AreaOpacity
parameters.description: Area charts only: optional 0–1 opacity override for solid area fills. Null keeps the light/dark --tm-chart-area-fill-opacity design token; gradient areas retain their stop-based opacity.

parameters.name: InteractiveLegend
parameters.description: When true, legend items become buttons that toggle the visibility of their series (multi-dataset legend) or single value (per-value legend). The component owns the hidden state; OnSeriesToggle reports each change. Default false keeps the legend non-interactive (backward compatible).

parameters.name: OnSeriesToggle
parameters.description: Raised whenever a legend series/value is toggled.

parameters.name: ShowTooltip

items.description: Shared base class for Tempo.Blazor components that standardises the data-testid convention. A component renders each of its internal test ids through the protected TestId(name) helper: when a host sets TestIdPrefix, every internal id becomes "{prefix}-{name}", so multiple instances of the same component on one page no longer collide; when the prefix is null the bare name is emitted, so existing E2E selectors keep working (fully backward compatible). DataTestId overrides the component's root test id and is resolved through the protected RootTestId(defaultName) helper. Inheriting this base is purely additive: both parameters are optional, default to null, and change no existing rendered output.

members.name: TestIdPrefix
members.description: Optional namespace applied to every internal test id the component emits via TestId(name). When set, each id becomes "{prefix}-{name}", letting several instances of the same component coexist on one page without colliding. Null emits bare names, preserving backward-compatible selectors.

examples.title: Reorderable board persisting position
examples.code:
<TmKanbanBoard TItem="TaskItem"
               Items="@tasks"
               Columns="@columns"
               ColumnSelector="t => t.Status"
               CardTemplate="RenderCard"
               OnItemMoved="HandleMove"
               OnItemReordered="HandleMove" />

@code {
    void HandleMove(KanbanMoveEvent<TaskItem> e)
    {
        var moved = e.Item with { Status = e.ToColumn };
        tasks.RemoveAll(t => t.Id == e.Item.Id);
        var at = e.TargetBeforeItem is not null
            ? tasks.FindIndex(t => t.Id == e.TargetBeforeItem.Id)
            : tasks.Count;
        tasks.Insert(at < 0 ? tasks.Count : at, moved);
    }
}

examples.title: Swimlanes grouped by assignee
examples.code:
<TmKanbanBoard TItem="TaskItem"
               Items="@tasks"
               Columns="@columns"
               ColumnSelector="t => t.Status"
               SwimlaneSelector="t => string.IsNullOrEmpty(t.Assignee) ? null : t.Assignee"
               CardTemplate="RenderCard"
               OnItemMoved="HandleMove"
               OnItemReordered="HandleReorder" />

@code {
    // e.ToSwimlane is the target assignee (null = unassigned / "no value" lane)
    void HandleMove(KanbanMoveEvent<TaskItem> e)
        => Apply(e, e.Item with { Status = e.ToColumn, Assignee = e.ToSwimlane ?? "" });
}

items.description:
Full-featured data grid with declarative column definitions, client-side and server-side data modes, sorting, inline column filters, global search, row selection with bulk actions, column visibility picker, drag-to-group with multi-level grouping, pagination with per-group mini-pager for server-side grouping, virtualized scrolling, external filter builder, and saved view management.\n\nComposition rule: either the owning page filters the data and the table renders a content-only surface (set ToolbarMode=ContentOnly and supply pre-filtered Items/DataProvider), or the table owns filtering via its own toolbar and external filter builder. Avoid enabling both filter surfaces at the same time unless they are explicitly integrated (e.g. the page reads the table's ActiveFilters).

Pagination test hooks: the paging footer carries data-testid="pagination-container" and the table's own item-range text "pagination-summary"; the embedded TmPagination contributes "pagination", "pagination-info", "pagination-prev", "pagination-next", "pagination-page-{n}" and "pagination-page-size". TestIdPrefix set on the table is propagated into the embedded pagination, so two tables on one page do not collide. Use PaginationAttributes for non-test attributes on the pagination root and PaginationInfoTemplate (context: DataTablePaginationInfo) to replace the built-in "showing X-Y of Z" wording.

parameters.name: CardMode
parameters.description: Opt-in responsive card mode. When true, the wrapper gains the tm-data-table-wrapper--card class and every data cell carries a data-label attribute (the owning column's Title), which the scoped CSS uses on narrow viewports to stack each row into a labeled card. Default: false — the rendered markup is unchanged from a non-card table, so existing consumers are unaffected. Fully compatible with server-side data (DataProvider) and sorting.

parameters.name: ChildContent
parameters.description: Column definitions (TmDataTableColumn children).

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class applied to the wrapper div.

parameters.name: CsvDelimiter
parameters.description: Delimiter used by the built-in CSV export. Defaults to a comma.

parameters.name: CurrentTenantId
parameters.description: Current tenant ID for tenant view scoping.

parameters.name: CurrentUserId
parameters.description: Current user ID for personal view scoping.

parameters.name: DataProvider
parameters.description: Server-side data provider. When set, overrides Items and calls GetDataAsync on query changes.

parameters.name: DefaultPageSize
parameters.description: Initial page size. Default: 25.

parameters.name: DetailTemplate
parameters.description: Template rendered as an expandable detail row beneath a data row.

parameters.name: DisplayResolver
parameters.description: Universal display resolver for field labels and filter values. DisplayResolver(fieldName, null) → localized field/column label (e.g., "Status" → "Stav") DisplayResolver(fieldName, rawValue) → localized value (e.g., ("Status","Active") → "Aktivní") Return null to use defaults (FilterDefinition.FieldLabel, column Title, or raw value). Set once on the component — flows to ViewManager, FilterBuilder, and ColumnPicker.

parameters.name: Editable
parameters.description: Enables inline row editing (double-click a row). Requires editable columns with EditTemplate.

parameters.name: EmptyTitle
parameters.description: Heading shown in the empty state when no items are available.

parameters.name: ExternalFilterDefinitions
parameters.description: Filter definitions for the inline external filter builder (shown above the table when ViewProvider is set). When the page owns filtering, leave this empty and set ShowExternalFilterBuilder to false or use ToolbarMode = ContentOnly.

parameters.name: GroupsCollapsedByDefault
parameters.description: Whether groups are collapsed by default.

parameters.name: IsLoading
parameters.description: When true, shows a loading spinner instead of rows. Useful for manual loading control.

parameters.name: Items
parameters.description: In-memory items. When set without DataProvider, client-side sort/filter/pagination applies.

parameters.name: LayoutChanged
parameters.description: Fires whenever the column layout (widths or pin state) changes.

parameters.name: LayoutStore
parameters.description: Persistence hook for per-user column layout (widths + pin state). Optional.

parameters.name: OnExportCompleted
parameters.description: Fires after an export has been generated and handed to the browser download API.

parameters.name: OnGroupingChanged
parameters.description: Fires when grouping configuration changes.

parameters.name: OnLoadDetail
parameters.description: Invoked once, the first time a row is expanded, so the host can lazily load detail data before DetailTemplate renders it.

parameters.name: OnRowClick
parameters.description: Fires when a data row is clicked.

parameters.name: OnRowCommit
parameters.description: Invoked to persist a committed row edit. Return false to keep the row in edit mode (for example when a server rejected the change). When null, the edit commits locally.

parameters.name: OnRowEditCancel
parameters.description: Fires when a row edit is cancelled. The callback receives the edited item; restoring its original values is the consuming application's responsibility.

parameters.name: OnRowEditCancelled
parameters.description: Legacy cancellation callback invoked after OnRowEditCancel. It receives the already-mutated item; restoring original values remains the consuming application's responsibility.

parameters.name: OnRowEditStart
parameters.description: Fires when a row enters inline edit mode.

parameters.name: OnRowSave
parameters.description: Fires after a valid row edit is saved.

parameters.name: OnSelectionChanged
parameters.description: Fires when the selection changes.

parameters.name: PageSizeOptions
parameters.description: Page size options shown in the pagination dropdown.

parameters.name: PaginationAttributes
parameters.description: Additional HTML attributes splatted onto the built-in TmPagination root element. Use it to attach host-owned hooks (analytics ids, extra ARIA) to the pagination bar; the data-testids of the pagination controls themselves come from TestIdPrefix, which this table propagates to the pagination automatically.

parameters.name: PaginationInfoTemplate
parameters.description: Replaces the built-in "showing X–Y of Z" summary next to the pagination bar. The context carries the current paging state (DataTablePaginationInfo), so a host can render its own wording instead of the library's TmDataTable_ShowingItems resource. When null the localized default is used.

parameters.name: RowAttributes
parameters.description: Optional row-level HTML attributes applied to every data row, including non-virtualized, virtualized, and grouped leaf rows.

parameters.name: RowEditValidator
parameters.description: Optional validator content rendered inside the row's cascading EditContext while editing (for example <FluentValidationValidator /> or <DataAnnotationsValidator />). Commit is blocked while the edit context is invalid.

parameters.name: RowValidatorFactory
parameters.description: Optional factory that creates the EditContext cascaded to a row's edit templates. When omitted, the table creates a context for the edited item.

parameters.name: ScrollMode
parameters.description: Scroll/pagination mode. Default: Pagination.

parameters.name: SearchText
parameters.description: Controlled search text. When set, the component uses this value instead of its internal state.

parameters.name: SearchTextChanged
parameters.description: Fires when the search text changes.

parameters.name: Selectable
parameters.description: Enables row checkboxes for multi-select.

parameters.name: SelectionActions
parameters.description: Render fragment shown in the selection action bar (bulk actions).

parameters.name: ShowColumnMenu
parameters.description: Whether column header controls (pin toggle, resize handle) are shown. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowColumnPicker
parameters.description: When true, shows the column visibility picker. Default: true.

parameters.name: ShowEditButtons
parameters.description: Whether to show the row edit action buttons. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: ShowExport
parameters.description: Shows the export format dropdown in the table toolbar. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: ShowExternalFilterBuilder
parameters.description: When true and a ViewProvider is set, shows the inline FilterBuilder for external filtering. Default: true. Set to false when the surrounding page owns the filtering UI to avoid duplicate filters.

parameters.name: ShowGrouping
parameters.description: Whether to show the grouping drop zone above the table.

parameters.name: ShowPagination
parameters.description: When true, shows the TmPagination bar when more than one page exists. Default: true. When false, a client-side table (Items) renders every item it was handed rather than the first page — the pager is the only element that reaches pages 2..N, so hiding it and still slicing would leave the remaining rows in no element at all. Server-side paging through DataProvider is unaffected: there the page is chosen by the provider.

parameters.name: ShowSearch
parameters.description: When true, shows the global search input. Default: true.

parameters.name: ShowToolbar
parameters.description: When true, renders the toolbar container with search, column picker, and view manager. Default: true. The toolbar is not rendered when no visible control would be shown (see ToolbarMode). For a page-owned filter surface, set ToolbarMode to ContentOnly and supply filtered data via Items or DataProvider.

parameters.name: ShowViewManager
parameters.description: When true and a ViewProvider is set, renders the TmViewManager. Default: true.

parameters.name: ToolbarMode
parameters.description: High-level preset that controls which toolbar chrome elements are rendered. Full respects the individual Show* booleans; other modes override them.

parameters.name: ViewCanCreateTenantViews
parameters.description: Whether the user can create tenant-wide views. Default: false.

parameters.name: ViewContext
parameters.description: Unique identifier for this table instance. Used to scope saved views to specific tables (e.g., "employees", "projects").

parameters.name: ViewFilterDefinitions
parameters.description: Filter definitions used by the view manager filter builder when creating or editing saved views.

parameters.name: ViewProvider
parameters.description: Optional view persistence provider. When set, enables saved views and (by default) the external filter builder. Use ShowExternalFilterBuilder = false to keep saved views without rendering the inline filter builder, or ToolbarMode = ContentOnly when the page owns the filtering UI.

parameters.name: VirtualItemSize
parameters.description: Height of a single row in pixels (required for Virtualize). Default: 48.

parameters.name: VirtualOverscanCount
parameters.description: Number of extra items to render above/below viewport. Default: 3.

parameters.name: VirtualScrollHeight
parameters.description: Fixed height for the virtualized scroll container (e.g. "600px", "80vh").

items.compositionGuidance: Either the page filters the data, or the table filters the data. When the page owns the filters, use ToolbarMode=ContentOnly and do not set ViewProvider/ExternalFilterDefinitions. When the table owns the filters, use the default Full toolbar mode and optionally a ViewProvider.

examples.code:

               ViewContext="orders"
               OnViewApplied="ApplyView"
               GetCurrentView="GetCurrentTableView"
               AvailableColumns="@availableColumns"
               FilterDefinitions="@filterDefs"
               DisplayResolver="ResolveDisplay"
               CanCreateTenantViews="true"
               CurrentUserId="@userId"
               CurrentTenantId="@tenantId" />

@code {
    // DisplayResolver flows from TmViewManager → TmFilterBuilder → TmFilterChip.
    // Usually you set DisplayResolver on the parent TmDataTable or TmMultiViewList
    // and it flows automatically. Direct usage shown here for standalone scenarios.
    private string? ResolveDisplay(string fieldName, string? rawValue)
    {
        if (rawValue is null)
            return fieldName switch { "Status" => "Order Status", "Priority" => "Priority", _ => null };
        return (fieldName, rawValue) switch
        {
            ("Status", "Pending") => "Pending",
            ("Status", "Shipped") => "Shipped",

    ParentPlaceholder="Select region..."
    ChildPlaceholder="Select city..."
    @bind-ParentValue="_region"
    @bind-ChildValue="_city"
    LoadChildOptionsAsync="LoadCitiesAsync" />

@code {
    private string? _region;
    private string? _city;

    private async Task<IReadOnlyList<SelectOption<string>>> LoadCitiesAsync(string? region)
    {
        if (region is null) return [];
        var cities = await _locationService.GetCitiesAsync(region);
        return cities.Select(c => new SelectOption<string>(c.Id, c.Name)).ToList();
    }
}

items.description: Grouped currency input combining a decimal amount field, a currency select, and an optional read-only converted-amount field. Conversion is opt-in via the ConvertAsync callback — when null, the converted column is hidden. Supports a manual exchange rate override and full read-only mode. All labels are localizable.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: The entered amount.

parameters.name: AmountChanged
parameters.description: Fires when Amount changes.

parameters.name: AmountLabel
parameters.description: Override label for the amount field.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class.

parameters.name: ConvertAsync
parameters.description: Optional async callback for converting Amount to another currency. Receives (amount, currencyCode) and returns the converted value. Used as a fallback when ExchangeRateProvider is not supplied. When both this and ExchangeRateProvider are null, the converted amount column is hidden entirely.

parameters.name: ConvertedAmount
parameters.description: Result of the conversion. Bind this to receive updates from the component.

parameters.name: ConvertedAmountChanged
parameters.description: Fires when ConvertedAmount changes.

parameters.name: ConvertedLabel
parameters.description: Override label for the converted amount field.

parameters.name: Currencies
parameters.description: Available currency options shown in the select.

parameters.name: Currency
parameters.description: Selected currency code (e.g. "USD").

parameters.name: CurrencyChanged
parameters.description: Fires when Currency changes.

parameters.name: CurrencyLabel
parameters.description: Override label for the currency select.

parameters.name: ExchangeRateProvider
parameters.description: Optional exchange-rate provider. When supplied, it takes precedence over ConvertAsync: the component fetches the rate for Currency → TargetCurrency and multiplies the amount by it. If the provider returns null (rate unavailable), the converted value is left unchanged. When null, the existing ConvertAsync callback is used exactly as before.

parameters.name: ManualRate
parameters.description: Manual exchange rate override.

parameters.name: ManualRateChanged
parameters.description: Fires when ManualRate changes.

parameters.name: ManualRateLabel
parameters.description: Override label for the manual rate field.

parameters.name: ReadOnly
parameters.description: Makes all fields read-only.

parameters.name: ShowManualRate
parameters.description: Show the manual exchange rate input. Only meaningful when ConvertAsync is provided.

parameters.name: TargetCurrency
parameters.description: Target currency code the amount is converted into when using ExchangeRateProvider. When null, the selected Currency is used as the target (a self-conversion). Ignored by the callback-based ConvertAsync path, which encodes its own target.

examples.title: Basic — amount + currency only
examples.code:
<TmCurrencyInput Currencies="@_currencies"
    @bind-Amount="_amount"
    @bind-Currency="_currency" />

examples.title: With async conversion
examples.code:
<TmCurrencyInput Currencies="@_currencies"
    @bind-Amount="_amount"
    @bind-Currency="_currency"
    @bind-ConvertedAmount="_converted"
    ConvertAsync="ConvertToCzkAsync"
    ConvertedLabel="Amount (CZK)" />

@code {
    private async Task<decimal?> ConvertToCzkAsync(decimal amount, string currency)
    {
        var rate = await _rateService.GetRateAsync(currency, "CZK");
        return rate is null ? null : Math.Round(amount * rate.Value, 2);
    }
}

examples.title: With manual rate override
examples.code:
<TmCurrencyInput Currencies="@_currencies"
    @bind-Amount="_amount"
    @bind-Currency="_currency"
    @bind-ConvertedAmount="_converted"
    @bind-ManualRate="_manualRate"
    ConvertAsync="ConvertToCzkAsync"
    ShowManualRate="true" />

examples.title: Read-only display
examples.code:
<TmCurrencyInput Currencies="@_currencies"
    Amount="1500"
    Currency="EUR"
    ReadOnly="true" />

items.description: Culture-aware decimal input. Accepts both comma and dot as the decimal separator, cleans pasted text (currency symbols, units, thousands separators), formats the value on blur for the chosen culture, rounds to DecimalPlaces, supports Min/Max/Step with +/- steppers and ArrowUp/ArrowDown keys, offers a percent mode (the model keeps the fraction while the field shows the percentage), and reports DataAnnotations validation messages when used inside an EditForm.

parameters.name: AutoComplete
parameters.description: HTML autocomplete attribute. Common values: "on", "off".

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) applied to the wrapper.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: Culture used for parsing and formatting. Defaults to CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.

parameters.name: DecimalPlaces
parameters.description: Number of fractional digits used for display and for rounding the committed value (clamped to 0-28).

parameters.name: Disabled
parameters.description: Disable the input.

parameters.name: Error
parameters.description: Error message. When set, it wins over any validation message coming from the surrounding EditContext, replaces the help text and marks the field invalid.

parameters.name: HelpText
parameters.description: Help text rendered below the input.

parameters.name: Id
parameters.description: Explicit id of the input element. When omitted, a unique id is generated so the label stays associated.

parameters.name: Label
parameters.description: Field label.

parameters.name: Max
parameters.description: Largest allowed value, on the displayed scale (in percent mode, Min="0" ... Max="100" means 0-100 %).

parameters.name: Min
parameters.description: Smallest allowed value, on the displayed scale (in percent mode, Min="0" ... Max="100" means 0-100 %).

parameters.name: Percent
parameters.description: Percent mode: Value holds the fraction (0.15) while the input shows and accepts the percentage (15). Min, Max and Step also work on the percentage scale, and a "%" suffix is added unless Suffix says otherwise.

parameters.name: Placeholder
parameters.description: Placeholder text shown while the input is empty.

parameters.name: Prefix
parameters.description: Prefix text rendered before the input (e.g. "EUR").

parameters.name: ReadOnly
parameters.description: Render the input as read-only.

parameters.name: Required
parameters.description: Marks the input as required. Shows a required marker on the label and sets aria-required on the input element.

parameters.name: ShowButtons
parameters.description: Show the +/- stepper buttons.

parameters.name: Step
parameters.description: Amount added or removed by the steppers and the arrow keys, on the displayed scale (default 1 — in percent mode, one percentage point).

parameters.name: Suffix
parameters.description: Suffix text rendered after the input (e.g. "/ pc").

parameters.name: UseGrouping
parameters.description: Show thousands separators while the field is not being edited (default true).

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Current decimal value. null when the input is empty or holds unparsable text.

parameters.name: ValueChanged
parameters.description: Fires when the committed value changes (on change/blur, not on every keystroke).

parameters.name: ValueExpression
parameters.description: Expression identifying the bound model field. Blazor supplies it automatically when you use @bind-Value; it is what links the input to DataAnnotationsValidator messages inside an EditForm.

examples.title: TQL query field with autocomplete, error underlines and submit
examples.code:
<TmQueryInput @bind-Value="_query"
              Label="Filter"
              Placeholder="status = Active AND priority IN (High, Critical)"
              SuggestionsProvider="SuggestAsync"
              Errors="_errors"
              OnSubmit="RunQuery" />

@code {
    string? _query;
    IReadOnlyList<QueryErrorSpan> _errors = [];

    Task<IReadOnlyList<QuerySuggestion>> SuggestAsync(QuerySuggestionRequest req)

examples.title: Basic user picker
examples.code:
<TmUserPicker TUser="UserDto"
    @bind-Value="_ownerLogin"
    SearchProvider="SearchUsersAsync"
    ResolveProvider="ResolveUserAsync"
    ValueSelector="@(u => u.Login)"
    DisplaySelector="@(u => u.DisplayName)"
    Label="Owner"
    Placeholder="Search people..." />

@code {
    private string? _ownerLogin;

    private async Task<TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>> SearchUsersAsync(string query, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        try
        {
            var users = await UserService.SearchAsync(query, ct);
            return new TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>(users, users.Count == 0 ? TmPickerFetchState.Empty : TmPickerFetchState.Ok);
        }
        catch (Exception) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            return new TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>([], TmPickerFetchState.Transient);
        }
    }

    private async Task<TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>> ResolveUserAsync(string login, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        try
        {
            var user = await UserService.GetByLoginAsync(login, ct);
            return new TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>(user, TmPickerFetchState.Ok);
        }
        catch (Exception) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            return new TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>(default, TmPickerFetchState.Transient);
        }
    }
}

items.description: Guards a form or working area against losing unsaved changes. Registers a router LocationChanging handler so internal navigation while dirty shows a TmDialog confirmation instead of navigating away silently, and optionally arms a browser beforeunload prompt for tab close/refresh. Does not manage locks or working copies itself — it only gates navigation.

parameters.name: BeforeUnloadPrompt
parameters.description: When true, also registers a browser beforeunload prompt for tab close/refresh. The handler reads a client-cached dirty flag synchronously and never attempts a server call from inside unload.

parameters.name: CancelText
parameters.description: Text for the button that cancels navigation and stays on the page.

parameters.name: ConfirmLeaveText
parameters.description: Text for the button that confirms leaving (discarding unsaved work).

parameters.name: ConfirmMessage
parameters.default: "You have unsaved changes. If you leave now, they will be lost."
parameters.description: Message shown in the leave-confirmation dialog.

parameters.name: ConfirmTitle
parameters.description: Title shown in the leave-confirmation dialog.

parameters.name: Enabled
parameters.description: When false, the guard never blocks navigation or arms the browser unload prompt.

parameters.name: IsDirty
parameters.description: Whether the host currently has unsaved work. Ignored when IsDirtyCallback is set.

parameters.name: IsDirtyCallback
parameters.description: Optional callback evaluated on every navigation check instead of IsDirty. Useful when dirty state is derived (e.g. from a working copy) rather than tracked as a simple flag.

parameters.name: OnCancel
parameters.description: Raised after the user cancels and stays on the page.

parameters.name: OnConfirmLeave
parameters.description: Raised after the user confirms leaving, right before navigation is re-issued.

parameters.name: OnSaveAndLeave
parameters.description: Optional callback that persists the pending work before navigation continues. When set, the confirmation dialog shows a third "save and leave" button. RETURN TRUE ONLY WHEN THE WORK IS PERSISTED: on true the guard re-issues the blocked navigation, on false it navigates nowhere and leaves the dialog open, so a failed save cannot discard the very changes the guard exists to protect. Until 2.8.16 this was an EventCallback and the guard left regardless of the outcome.

parameters.name: SaveAndLeaveText
parameters.description: Text for the optional third button that saves the pending work and then leaves. The button is only rendered when OnSaveAndLeave is set, so existing two-choice usages are unchanged.

parameters.name: ShouldGuard
parameters.description: Optional predicate over the target URI deciding whether a navigation should be guarded at all. Return false to let a navigation through without prompting even when the host is dirty (e.g. moving between URL tabs or the detail↔sub-page of the same document). When null, every navigation is guarded.

examples.title: Guard a form with a working-copy dirty flag
examples.code:
<TmNavigationGuard IsDirty="@_isDirty"
                    OnConfirmLeave="@(() => _isDirty = false)" />

<EditForm Model="@_model" OnValidSubmit="Save">
    <TmTextInput @bind-Value="_model.Name" ValueChanged="@(v => { _model.Name = v; _isDirty = true; })" />
    <TmButton Type="ButtonType.Submit">Save</TmButton>
</EditForm>

examples.title: Derived dirty state via callback
examples.code: <TmNavigationGuard IsDirtyCallback="@(() => WorkingCopy.HasPendingChanges)" />

examples.title: Suppress the guard for a post-commit programmatic navigation
examples.code:
<TmNavigationGuard @ref="_guard" IsDirty="@_isDirty" />

@code {
    private TmNavigationGuard? _guard;

    private async Task SaveAndCloseAsync()
    {
        await SaveAsync();
        _isDirty = false;
        _guard?.Suppress();
        Navigation.NavigateTo("/documents");
    }
}

                    ConfirmTitle="Discard changes?"
                    ConfirmMessage="Your edits have not been saved yet."
                    ConfirmLeaveText="Discard"
                    CancelText="Keep editing" />

items.description: Tab strip component with Line, Pill, and Enclosed visual variants. Supports icons, badges, disabled tabs, and keyboard arrow-key navigation. Use with TmTabPanel children.

parameters.name: ActiveTabId
parameters.description: ID of the currently active tab.

parameters.name: ActiveTabIdChanged
parameters.description: Fires when the active tab changes.

parameters.name: ChildContent
parameters.description: Tab panel children.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class.

parameters.name: HeaderLeading
parameters.description: Optional content rendered immediately BEFORE the tab strip, as a SIBLING of the role="tablist" element — never inside it. The tab strip owns a roving tabindex (Arrow/Home/End, tabindex 0/-1, aria-selected AND the DOM focus, which moves with the selection); an element that can never be selected would misreport that contract to assistive technology and would be reachable with the arrow keys as if it were a tab. Setting this (or HeaderTrailing) wraps the strip in an extra .tm-tabs__header-row flex row. The wrapper is emitted ONLY when at least one slot is supplied; with neither slot the rendered markup is byte-identical to a tab strip that has no slots at all, so existing CSS and tests that rely on .tm-tabs > .tm-tabs__header keep working. CONTRACT FOR STICKY CONSUMERS: when the slots are in use, a sticky tab strip must stick the ROW (.tm-tabs__header-row), not the header (.tm-tabs__header). Sticking the header alone pins only the strip and lets the slot content scroll away.

parameters.name: HeaderTrailing
parameters.description: Optional content rendered immediately AFTER the tab strip, as a SIBLING of the role="tablist" element — never inside it, for the same roving-focus reason as HeaderLeading. Setting this (or HeaderLeading) wraps the strip in an extra .tm-tabs__header-row flex row. The wrapper is emitted ONLY when at least one slot is supplied; with neither slot the rendered markup is byte-identical to a tab strip that has no slots at all. CONTRACT FOR STICKY CONSUMERS: when the slots are in use, stick the ROW (.tm-tabs__header-row), not the header (.tm-tabs__header), otherwise the slot content scrolls away from under the pinned strip.

parameters.name: Variant
parameters.description: Visual variant of the tab strip.

parameters.name: Wrap
parameters.description: When true, the tab strip wraps onto multiple rows to fit the available width instead of scrolling horizontally. Use when many tabs would otherwise overflow/truncate in a narrow container.

@code {
    private TmSpreadsheet _spreadsheet = null!;

    private async Task OnFileSelected(InputFileChangeEventArgs e)
    {
        using var stream = e.File.OpenReadStream(5 * 1024 * 1024);
        using var ms = new MemoryStream();
        await stream.CopyToAsync(ms);
        await _spreadsheet.ImportFromExcelAsync(ms.ToArray());
    }

    private async Task ExportAsync()
    {
        var data = await _spreadsheet.ExportToExcelAsync();
        // download bytes...
    }
}

@code {
    private async Task HandleItemsDrop(TreeDropEventArgs<string> args)
    {
        // args.TargetNode — the node that was dropped onto
        // args.DraggedIds — IDs of the dragged items
        await MoveItemsToSuiteAsync(args.DraggedIds, args.TargetNode.Id);
    }
}

            Nodes="@_suites"

@code {
    private async Task HandleNodeMove(TreeNodeMoveEventArgs<string> args)
    {
        // args.MovedNode  — the node that was dragged
        // args.NewParent  — null when promoted to root
        await ReparentAsync(args.MovedNode.Id, args.NewParent?.Id);
        _suites = await LoadTreeAsync();
    }
}

libraryExamples.title: Custom Icon Registration
libraryExamples.description: Register custom application-specific icons via IconRegistry in Program.cs. Icons can be registered individually with inline SVG content, or in bulk via a custom IIconProvider implementation.

libraryExamples.title: Custom Localization — Full Language Override
libraryExamples.description: Replace all component UI strings with your own translations by implementing ITmLocalizer. Register your implementation AFTER AddTempoBlazor() so TryAddSingleton is skipped. The library has 500+ keys following the Tm[Component]_[Action] naming pattern.
libraryExamples.setupNote: ITmLocalizer is defined in Tempo.Blazor.Abstractions (namespace Tempo.Blazor.Localization). The interface has two indexer overloads: this[string key] for simple lookups and this[string key, params object[] arguments] for formatted strings. Keys follow the pattern Tm[ComponentName]_[Action]. Always return the key itself as fallback for unmapped keys to avoid blank UI. Use string.Format for keys with placeholders like TmDataTable_ShowingItems ({0}–{1} of {2}).

libraryExamples.title: Custom Localization — Partial Override (Decorator)
libraryExamples.description: Override only specific localization strings while keeping the rest from the built-in English/Czech resources. Uses a decorator pattern wrapping the default IStringLocalizer<TmResources>.
libraryExamples.setupNote: This approach injects IStringLocalizer<TmResources> (from the built-in .resx files) into your custom localizer. Only the keys in the _overrides dictionary are changed; everything else comes from the default resources. This works with both English and Czech — the built-in IStringLocalizer respects the current CultureInfo.

libraryExamples.title: Switching UI Language at Runtime

libraryExamples.setupNote: Built-in languages: 'en' (English, default) and 'cs' (Czech). Set the culture in Program.cs for initial language, or switch at runtime with a page reload. The DefaultTmLocalizer uses IStringLocalizer<TmResources> which respects DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture.

libraryExamples.title: TmNavigationGuard - Guard an edit form against unsaved-work loss
libraryExamples.description: Blocks internal router navigation while a form is dirty, showing a TmDialog confirmation, and arms a browser beforeunload prompt for tab close/refresh. Call Suppress() before a post-commit programmatic navigation so the guard does not re-prompt for work that was just saved.
libraryExamples.code:
<TmNavigationGuard @ref="_guard" IsDirty="@_isDirty" OnConfirmLeave="@(() => _isDirty = false)" />

<EditForm Model="@_model" OnValidSubmit="SaveAndCloseAsync">
    <TmTextInput @bind-Value="_model.Name"
        ValueChanged="@(v => { _model.Name = v; _isDirty = true; })" />
    <TmButton Type="ButtonType.Submit">Save</TmButton>
</EditForm>

@code {
    private TmNavigationGuard? _guard;
    private bool _isDirty;
    private DocumentModel _model = new();

    private async Task SaveAndCloseAsync()
    {
        await DocumentService.SaveAsync(_model);
        _isDirty = false;
        _guard?.Suppress();
        Navigation.NavigateTo("/documents");
    }
}
libraryExamples.setupNote: The beforeunload handler caches the dirty flag client-side and never calls back into .NET during unload, so it stays reliable even when the circuit is unloading. The guard only gates navigation — it does not manage locks or working copies.

libraryExamples.title: TmUserPicker - Generic picker with distinct empty vs transient-error states
libraryExamples.description: A generic entity picker (TUser) with debounced cancellable search and three explicit fetch states. A real network failure renders a retry-affordance error, never a silent "no results" message.
libraryExamples.code:
<TmUserPicker TUser="UserDto"
    @bind-Value="_ownerLogin"
    SearchProvider="SearchUsersAsync"
    ResolveProvider="ResolveUserAsync"
    ValueSelector="@(u => u.Login)"
    DisplaySelector="@(u => u.DisplayName)"
    Label="Owner"
    MinChars="2" />

@code {
    private string? _ownerLogin;

    private async Task<TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>> SearchUsersAsync(string query, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        try
        {
            var users = await UserService.SearchAsync(query, ct);
            return new TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>(users, users.Count == 0 ? TmPickerFetchState.Empty : TmPickerFetchState.Ok);
        }
        catch (Exception) when (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)
        {
            // A real outage — must NOT render as "no results".
            return new TmPickerSearchResult<UserDto>([], TmPickerFetchState.Transient);
        }
    }

    private async Task<TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>> ResolveUserAsync(string login, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var user = await UserService.GetByLoginAsync(login, ct);
        return new TmPickerResolveResult<UserDto>(user, TmPickerFetchState.Ok);
    }
}
libraryExamples.setupNote: SearchProvider/ResolveProvider are plain async functions — the component does not retry internally. If a caller wants retry-with-backoff before surfacing Transient, implement that inside the provider function itself.

package.title: Tempo.Blazor.Maps
package.description: Leaflet powered interactive map components for Tempo.Blazor with bundled OpenStreetMap tiles support, Canvas-rendered marker batches, and marker clustering.

gettingStarted.title: Tempo.Blazor.Maps
gettingStarted.overview: Leaflet powered interactive map components for Tempo.Blazor with bundled OpenStreetMap tiles support, Canvas-rendered marker batches, and marker clustering.

items.description: Interactive Leaflet map with OpenStreetMap tiles. Leaflet 1.9.4 and leaflet.markercluster 1.5.3 are bundled with the package (no CDN dependency) and loaded lazily by the ES module. Marker batches render through a Canvas renderer; data sets (markers/clusters) are swapped atomically. Supports client-side clustering, server-side aggregated cluster bubbles, and an optional IMapDataProvider with debounced, cancellable viewport loading.

parameters.name: CenterLatitude
parameters.description: Latitude of the initial map center in decimal degrees. Defaults to the Czech Republic centroid.

parameters.name: CenterLongitude
parameters.description: Longitude of the initial map center in decimal degrees. Defaults to the Czech Republic centroid.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS classes applied to the root element.

parameters.name: ClusterPoints
parameters.description: Server-side aggregated cluster points rendered as count bubbles. A cluster with Count = 1 renders as a plain marker. Replacing the list atomically re-renders all clusters.

parameters.name: DataProvider
parameters.description: Optional data source: when set, the component requests fresh points after the viewport settles (debounced by DataRequestDebounceMs), cancelling the superseded request. The component stays fully usable without a provider (imperative mode).

parameters.name: DataRequestDebounceMs
parameters.description: Debounce interval in milliseconds for provider requests after pan/zoom. Defaults to 300.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: CSS height of the map container (any CSS length). Defaults to 400px.

parameters.name: Markers
parameters.description: Markers rendered on the map via the Canvas renderer. Markers with a duplicate non-null Id are de-duplicated (the first occurrence wins). Replacing the list atomically re-renders all markers.

parameters.name: MaxZoom
parameters.description: Maximum zoom level offered by the tile layer. Defaults to 19.

parameters.name: OnClusterClick
parameters.description: Raised when a cluster is clicked: for server-side clusters the payload carries the cluster key and count; for client-side (markercluster) groups the key is null.

parameters.name: OnDataError
parameters.description: Raised when DataProvider throws; the map stays usable and keeps its last data.

parameters.name: OnMapClick
parameters.description: Raised when the map background is clicked. The payload carries the clicked coordinates and current zoom.

parameters.name: OnMarkerClick
parameters.description: Raised when a marker is clicked. The payload carries the marker id and coordinates.

parameters.name: OnZoomChanged
parameters.description: Raised after the zoom level changes. The payload carries the new center and zoom.

parameters.name: TileUrlTemplate
parameters.description: Tile layer URL template. Defaults to the public OpenStreetMap tile server.

parameters.name: UseClientClustering
parameters.description: When true, Markers are grouped client-side with leaflet.markercluster (spiderfy on max zoom, zoom-to-bounds on cluster click).

parameters.name: Zoom
parameters.description: Initial Leaflet zoom level. Fractional values are supported. Defaults to 7.5 (whole Czech Republic).

methods.name: SetViewAsync
methods.description: Moves the map to the given center and zoom without animation.

methods.name: GetViewportAsync
methods.description: Reads the current map center and zoom.

methods.name: SetMarkersAsync
methods.description: Atomically replaces all declarative data with the supplied marker batch (Canvas rendered).

methods.name: SetClusterPointsAsync
methods.description: Atomically replaces all declarative data with the supplied server-side cluster points.

methods.name: AddMarkersAsync
methods.description: Adds a batch of Canvas markers on top of the current content.

methods.name: AddClusterGroupAsync
methods.description: Creates an empty client-side cluster group (leaflet.markercluster) and returns its id.

methods.name: AddMarkerToClusterAsync
methods.description: Adds a single marker into a client-side cluster group.

methods.name: AddMarkersToClusterAsync
methods.description: Adds a batch of markers into a client-side cluster group.

methods.name: ClearMarkersAsync
methods.description: Removes all markers, cluster groups, and data layers from the map.

methods.name: InvalidateSizeAsync
methods.description: Recalculates the map size. Call after the map container becomes visible again (e.g. hidden tab).

methods.name: RefreshDataAsync
methods.description: Requests fresh data from DataProvider immediately (bypasses the debounce). No-op without a provider.

<TmMap CenterLatitude="49.8175"

       OnMarkerClick="HandleMarkerClick" />

items.description: Evaluates safe stencil binding expressions. The grammar is deliberately tiny: literals, bare identifiers that read the element's props, the built-ins size.w, size.h and repeat.index, arithmetic and comparison operators, ?? and ternary conditionals, and the single permitted function token(key, fallback). Any other call is a parse error. The public evaluation APIs never throw — an unparseable or nonsensical expression yields StencilValue.Null — so a broken stencil pack cannot take the editor down.

members.name: Evaluate
members.description: Parses and evaluates expression; malformed input returns the raw string and never throws.

examples.title: Use StencilEvaluator

items.description: A parsed safe binding expression. Public parsing APIs never throw on malformed input: they return a literal-mode instance with IsMalformed set to true. The only permitted function call is token(key); any other call becomes a parse error and is handled by the same literal fallback. Parse once and hand the instance to StencilEvaluator.Evaluate to avoid re-parsing in hot render paths.

items.description: Produces a clean, interaction-free SVG RenderFragment for a single WireframePage. This is the shared presentation layer reused by the live canvas and by headless server-side rendering (IWireframeSvgRenderer), so the visual stays in one place and previews cannot drift from the editor. It renders only presentation: the page <svg> root plus connector arrow markers (and an optional grid) in <defs>, the page background, visible connector paths and their labels, and each element as a translated inner-<svg> viewport hosting the component.

items.description: Pastes the internal clipboard into a target range with paste-special semantics: selectable content (values / formulas / formats / all / all-except-borders), an optional arithmetic operation against the existing target values, skip-blanks, and transpose. Relative formula references are shifted by the paste offset (except when transposing, where formulas are flattened to their computed value to avoid producing wrong references). Undo restores the overwritten cells exactly.

items.description: Removes duplicate rows from a range, keeping the first occurrence of each distinct key-column combination and compacting the surviving rows upward within the range. Only the columns inside the range are touched (Excel/OnlyOffice semantics); cells outside the range stay put. The whole operation is a single atomic step: Undo restores the original layout exactly. Ranges that intersect a merged cell are rejected.

examples.title: Basic spreadsheet
examples.code:
<TmSpreadsheet Height="500px"
               RowsCount="100"
               ColumnsCount="20"
               OnChange="HandleChange" />

@code {
    private void HandleChange(SpreadsheetChangeEventArgs args)
        => Console.WriteLine($"{args.CellRef} = {args.NewValue}");
}

examples.title: Load and export an XLSX workbook
examples.code:
<TmSpreadsheet @ref="_sheet" Data="@_xlsxBytes" />

<TmButton OnClick="DownloadAsync">Download</TmButton>

@code {
    private TmSpreadsheet? _sheet;
    private byte[]? _xlsxBytes;

    private async Task DownloadAsync()
    {
        var bytes = await _sheet!.ExportToExcelAsync();
        // hand the bytes to your download helper
    }
}

examples.title: Read-only view and programmatic edits
examples.code:
<TmSpreadsheet @ref="_sheet" Mode="SpreadsheetMode.Full" />

@code {
    private TmSpreadsheet? _sheet;

    protected override void OnAfterRender(bool firstRender)
    {
        if (!firstRender) return;
        _sheet!.SetCellValue("A1", "Total");
        _sheet.SetCellValue("B1", "=SUM(B2:B10)");
    }
}

R.4.8 / R.5.1 cutover bridge — converts a to/from the JS core-engine model (the { documentId, body: { blocks: [...] } } shape that coreEngine.createCoreEditor consumes). The hosted component (TmDocumentCoreEngineHost) sends to JS and rebuilds the document from on save. R.5.1 — full round-trip (no data loss on save). Round-trips paragraphs, headings, lists, quotes, text runs + inline marks, paragraph alignment, AND the structural blocks that previously vanished: tables (rows/cells/spans/header + nested blocks, recursively), images (standalone ↔ a paragraph carrying a drawing run, plus inline ), and page breaks. Rich C# content the engine does not model (image source/asset/link/natural-size, token/field/note runs) is carried verbatim in a __docSource preserve channel and restored on the way back, with the engine-managed visible fields (text/url/size/wrap/position/caption/alt) overlaid on top so user edits survive.

Pure C# service that recognises Notion-style markdown shortcut patterns typed at the beginning of a block line. Call Detect after the user presses Space or Enter, passing the full plain-text content of the current block including the trigger character. Matching is prefix-based, so the text after the trigger is returned in TextAfterTrigger. Recognised prefixes, most specific first: "### ", "## ", "# ", "- [x] ", "- [ ] ", "[x] ", "[ ] ", "[] ", "* ", "- ", "> ", plus any digits followed by ". " for a numbered list. The exact tokens "```" and "---" (Enter) become a Code block and a Divider. FromJsShortcutKey and IsCheckedTodo bridge the shortcut keys emitted by notion-editor.js to the C# type system.

items.description: Async undo / redo history for a single Notion editor instance. items.description: Top-level inline or linked database block. Renders an editable title and icon, a toolbar (filter, sort, group, sub-items, properties, import/export, and new-record with templates), view tabs, and the active view, loading fields, views, and records through the database provider.

Kanban board view that groups database records into columns by a select or status field. Renders cards with cover image, title, and preview properties, supports drag-and-drop between columns (which rewrites the group field), and offers per-column add-card.

Monthly calendar view (a six-week, Monday-based grid) that places records as colored events on their date field. Supports previous/next/today navigation, drag-to-reschedule, click-to-create, and per-cell overflow indicators.

Dispatcher that renders the matching type-specific cell editor for a database field based on its type (defaulting to text), forwarding the value, read-only and editing state, and the commit, cancel, and edit-request callbacks.
Editor for a checkbox (boolean) database cell that renders a checked or unchecked box and toggles the value on click.
Read-only display of a record's created-by database cell, showing the user's avatar initials and name.
Read-only display of a record's created-time database cell, formatted as a date with the full timestamp shown on hover.
Editor for a date database cell, displaying the formatted date (with time when the field includes it) and offering a date or datetime-local input.
Editor for an email database cell, showing the value as a mailto link and, when editing, an email input.
Read-only display of a files database cell, showing a file icon with the file value or a no-file placeholder.
Read-only display of a computed formula database cell, rendering the calculated value as text or a placeholder.
Read-only display of a record's last-edited-by database cell, showing the user's avatar initials and name.
Read-only display of a record's last-edited-time database cell, formatted as a date with the full timestamp shown on hover.
Editor for a multi-select database cell, showing selected values as colored chips and, when editing, a searchable popup to toggle and apply multiple options.
Editor for a number database cell, displaying the value formatted per the field's number format (currency, percent, thousands separators) and offering a numeric input that commits a parsed number.
Editor for a person database cell, showing an avatar with initials and the assigned person's name (or an unassigned placeholder), edited via a text input.
Editor for a phone database cell, showing the value as a tel link and, when editing, a telephone input.
Read-only display of a relation database cell, rendering linked record ids as chips or a no-linked-records placeholder.
Read-only display of a computed rollup database cell, rendering the aggregated value as text or a placeholder.
Editor for a single-select database cell, showing the chosen option as a colored chip and, when editing, a searchable popup to pick one option or clear it.
Editor for a status database cell, showing the selected option chip and, when editing, a searchable popup with options grouped by status group.
Editor for a text database cell, showing plain text and, when editing, an inline input that commits on Enter or blur and cancels on Escape.
Editor for a URL database cell, showing the value as an external link and, when editing, a URL input.

Dialog for editing a database field's name and type with type-specific configuration - select and multi-select options, status groups, number format, formula expression, relation target, rollup settings, and date format - plus duplicate and delete.

Filter builder for a database view. Renders condition rows (field, operator, and a type-appropriate value input) and nested AND/OR groups with add, remove, and clear-all, emitting the assembled filter.

Gallery view showing database records as a grid of cards with a cover image (from a cover or files field), title, and preview properties. Card size and cover fit are configurable, with an add-card button.
Grouping configuration panel for a database view, letting the user pick a groupable field, toggle hiding empty groups, and set the group sort direction.
Modal with Import and Export tabs for a database. Import uploads a CSV, previews it, and maps columns onto fields; export selects a view (or all records) and downloads CSV.
Compact list view of database records, rendering each as a clickable row with a page icon, primary title, and colored preview-field chips, plus an empty state and add-row buttons.

Modal detail view for a single database record with an editable primary title, property rows edited via TmNotionDbCell, and a nested page-block editor for the record's content, auto-saving through the database provider.
Sort configuration panel for a database view, listing sort rules (field plus ascending or descending) that can be added, removed, drag-reordered, and cleared.

Spreadsheet-style table view of a database. Renders a select-all header, resizable and drag-reorderable field columns with an add-field button, and grouped collapsible rows with inline per-cell editing (TmNotionDbCell), row selection, expandable sub-items, and add-row.
Modal for editing a database record template - its name and emoji, default field values (via TmNotionDbCell), and template content blocks - auto-saving through the database provider.
Popup listing a database's record templates. Each template can create a new record, with actions to add, edit, or delete templates.

Gantt-style timeline view with day/week/month zoom and an optional sidebar table. Positions records as horizontal bars from their start and end date fields, with drag to move or resize (updating the dates), a today marker, and period navigation.

Block embedding a Tempo diagram document. The empty editable state offers create and insert-existing actions; the filled state shows an SVG preview with an edit overlay that opens TmNotionDiagramEditModal, plus an editable caption and a not-found state.
Modal dialog hosting the dynamically loaded diagram editor (or a missing-package notice) with Save and Discard actions and a loading spinner while the document loads.
Renders a list of block-level diffs (added, removed, modified, moved) with per-block before and after HTML in either inline or side-by-side view mode, with loading and empty states.
Divider block — a focusable horizontal rule. Enter adds a Paragraph below; Backspace/Delete removes the block.

Renders one row of a TmNotionTableBlock as a <tr> of editable cells. Applies the header-row/header-column styling, the per-column horizontal alignment, cell background colours, merge spans, range-selection highlight, drag handles for row reordering, and Tab/Shift+Tab navigation across cells.

items.description: The result handed back to the host when the user applies a column mapping in TmImportWizard. This is a mapping payload, not a full import engine.

Server-side document layout contract: GenerateLayoutSnapshotJson lays out a DocumentEditorDocument with the SAME JavaScript layout chain the canvas editor paints with (the embedded headless bundle) and returns the schema v1 layout snapshot JSON — the exact contract of DocumentPdfExportRequest.LayoutSnapshotJson, consumable by TempoDocumentPdfRenderer for WYSIWYG-parity PDF output without a browser. Accepts an optional page-setup override (size/orientation/margins in points), the font faces the PDF renderer embeds (required — layout fails closed without them), and a tracked-changes display mode for redline printing. Implementations are engine-hosting details (JintDocumentLayoutEngine today, swappable for another JS host or a native port without touching consumers); register via AddTempoDocumentLayout().

Headless document rendering facade: one call takes a template (or plain document) plus token values and produces a WYSIWYG PDF (RenderPdfAsync = DocumentAssemblyService.Assemble → ITempoDocumentLayoutService → TempoDocumentPdfRenderer, incl. watermark and forensic watermark passthrough) or per-page PNG previews at a parametrizable DPI (RenderPageImagesAsync — visual feedback for agents, tests and preview tooling). Register via AddTempoDocumentServices().

ITempoDocumentLayoutService hosted in Jint: evaluates the embedded headless layout bundle once per pooled engine and calls its generateHeadlessLayoutSnapshotJson seam — one JSON request in (canvas model + Skia advance tables), one JSON result out, no .NET↔JS callbacks per glyph. Engines are pooled thread-safely and bounded by observed concurrency, so repeated MCP/preview traffic never allocates an engine per call (CreatedEngineCount exposes pooling diagnostics). Fail-closed: missing fonts, an unknown font family, an unmeasurable glyph, or a JS failure throw TempoDocumentLayoutException with diagnostics instead of degrading the layout silently. Measured 2026-07-19 (Jint 4.13, .NET 10, Debug): ≈2.2 s cold / ≈0.9 s warm for a 54-page document (≈17 ms/page warm).

members.name: CreatedEngineCount
members.description: Total Jint engines created so far — diagnostics for pooling behavior.

items.description: Access to the embedded headless document layout bundle — the canvas editor's layout chain (layout snapshot export → display list → pagination → line breaker/paragraph engine/font metrics) compiled into a single ESM artifact by scripts/build-document-editor.mjs (npm run build:document-editor). Server-side layout hosts evaluate this script to produce the exact layout snapshot the browser editor exports, giving WYSIWYG parity by construction without a C# port of the layout code. items.description: An image reference the headless pipeline needs an embeddable source for: the owning document id, the provider asset id (when asset-backed) and the original URL (never an already-embeddable data URI). Passed to TempoDocumentImageSourceResolver before layout.

Fail-closed headless layout error: thrown when a layout could not be produced with WYSIWYG parity — no fonts were provided, the document references font families the provided faces cannot resolve (UnknownFontFamilies), glyphs are missing from resolved faces (MissingGlyphs), or the JS engine failed. Carries the measurement diagnostics so callers can report exactly which font faces to provide.

Diagnostic record for a glyph the provided font faces cannot measure: the resolved font family whose advance table lacks the glyph and the Unicode code point of the unmeasurable character. Reported by TempoDocumentLayoutException.MissingGlyphs.

DI registration for the headless document layout service: AddTempoDocumentLayout() registers ITempoDocumentLayoutService backed by the pooled Jint host (JintDocumentLayoutEngine) as an idempotent singleton.
One rendered page preview from ITempoDocumentService.RenderPageImagesAsync: zero-based page index, raster dimensions in pixels and the PNG bytes.

Result of a headless PDF render: the PDF bytes, the laid-out page count, the layout snapshot JSON (schema v1) the PDF was rendered from — reusable for previews or diagnostics — and the forensic watermark timestamp actually stamped into the PDF when a forensic watermark was requested.

Request for the headless document facade: the template or plain document, optional token values for assembly (null renders the document as-is), export options (page setup, review display mode, watermark, forensic watermark), the font faces to measure and embed with (required for WYSIWYG-accurate output) and optional document id / file name.

Default ITempoDocumentService: composes the server-side document pipeline — document assembly (IF/ELSE conditional chains, repeating sections, computed expressions over token values), headless canvas layout (pooled Jint host) and Skia PDF/raster rendering with embedded fonts. The clock is injectable via TimeProvider, so assembly date functions (TODAY/DATEADD) and the forensic watermark timestamp are deterministic under test; a missing forensic timestamp is stamped from the injected clock rather than an uncontrolled UtcNow. RenderPdfAsync returns the PDF plus page count and the layout snapshot JSON it was rendered from; RenderPageImagesAsync rasters every page to PNG at the requested DPI (96 = CSS pixel scale).

DI registration for the headless document facade: AddTempoDocumentServices() registers the full pipeline — ITempoDocumentLayoutService (pooled Jint host) and the ITempoDocumentService facade (assembly → layout → PDF / PNG previews) — as idempotent singletons; the facade resolves a registered TimeProvider when present, otherwise uses the system clock.

Precomputed glyph metrics for one font face in font design units (unhinted, linear): Unicode-keyed advance widths, ascent/descent/line gap, units-per-em and the missing-glyph advance. Produced by TempoFontAdvanceTableExtractor from the same TTF/OTF bytes the PDF renderer embeds; code points the font has no glyph for are omitted so the JS measurer can fall back to synthetic metrics with diagnostics.

Extracts glyph advance tables and vertical metrics from ReportPdfFontFace bytes via SkiaSharp (SKTypeface/SKFont with unhinted linear metrics at font-unit scale) and serializes them into the compact JSON the headless JS layout bundle measures with (createAdvanceFontMetricsService). Because the tables come from the SAME font bytes the PDF renderer embeds, headless measurement and PDF drawing agree by construction — no .NET↔JS callbacks per glyph. Default coverage: Basic Latin, Latin-1, Latin Extended-A/B (Czech and Central European diacritics), general punctuation and the euro sign; extendable via additionalCodePoints. Extraction is cached per face (family, weight, style, content hash) behind a thread-safe lazy cache; use the Shared instance for process-wide reuse.

Server-side image resolution seam for the headless facade (TempoDocumentRenderRequest.ImageResolver): resolves an image reference (asset id / URL) to an embeddable data URI before layout, so headless exports embed real images — the counterpart of the browser's IDocumentImageUrlResolver. Return null to leave the reference unresolved; its footprint then renders as a placeholder rectangle. Hosts should prefer asset-backed images for server-rendered exports; host-relative URLs are not resolvable on the server.
